items.title: aioovh
items.text:
aioovh, every OVHcloud API in Python, fully async and strongly typed.

Documentation: https://aioovh.businessagile.eu

Source Code: https://gitlab.com/businessagile/libraries/aioovh

aioovh is a client for the OVHcloud APIs, versions 1.0 and v2, organised around what you manipulate (bills, servers, domains, Public Cloud instances) rather than the API's paths. It is async from end to end, strongly typed, and covers every published API, not only the popular ones.

aioovh is based on Python type annotations, and powered by Pydantic, httpx2, whenever and stamina.

The key features are:

  • Async first: the official ovh package is synchronous and blocks the event loop; aioovh awaits every request on one HTTP client.
  • Business areas: compute, billing, domains, email, telecom... the same areas as its sibling aioscaleway. /me disappears: bills are in billing, SSH keys in iam.
  • References and objects: ovh.billing.bills(bill_id) acts without reading the bill first, await loads it, and a loaded bill is still a reference.
  • Collections: async for loads the objects behind a list of identifiers, a few at a time, or follows the v2 cursor; filter() narrows, ids() skips the loading.
  • Signed for you: the $1$ signature on the exact URL and body sent, the clock offset read once, or OAuth2 client credentials.
  • No API version in any name, and Public Cloud resources scoped by project, with a default.
  • Complete: generated from the schemas the API serves, 88 APIs and about 7,300 operations, each reachable.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
A recent and currently supported version of Python: 3.12 or later.

OVHcloud API credentials, an application key, secret and consumer key, or OAuth2 client credentials, given as arguments or read from the OVH_* variables of the official package.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
$ pip install aioovh
---> 100%
Successfully installed aioovh httpx2 pydantic pydantic-settings stamina whenever

items.title: Connect
items.text:
from aioovh import OVH

ovh = OVH(
    endpoint="ovh-eu",
    application_key="...",
    application_secret="...",
    consumer_key="...",
    default_project="...",
)

Every value left out is read from OVH_ENDPOINT, OVH_APPLICATION_KEY, OVH_APPLICATION_SECRET, OVH_CONSUMER_KEY and the other variables of the official package.

items.title: Bills and their lines
items.text:
from whenever import Date

async with ovh:
    async for bill in ovh.billing.bills.filter(date_from=Date(2026, 10, 1)):
        print(bill.bill_id, bill.date, bill.price_without_tax.value)
        async for line in bill.details:
            print("  ", line.description, line.total_price.value)

The 1.0 API lists bills as identifiers; iterating the collection loads each bill, a few at a time.

items.title: Act without loading
items.text:
await ovh.compute.vps("vps-1234.vps.ovh.net").reboot()
account = await ovh.account

items.title: Public Cloud
items.text:
async for instance in ovh.compute.instances.filter(project=project_id):
    print(instance.name, instance.status)

Without project, the client's default_project is used.

items.title: Editor support everywhere
items.text: Arguments, fields and results are typed, and checked with mypy --strict. Dates are whenever.Instant and whenever.Date, enumerations are open so that a value OVHcloud adds later does not break your code.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: The conventions shared with aioscaleway are in the Business Agile conventions (backend/08-python-api-clients.md, draft in /opt/businessagile/libraries/conventions-clients-api.md). This file covers what is specific to OVHcloud.

items.title: Two layers
items.text:
• Operations (src/aioovh/_operations/v1/<api>/, .../v2/<api>/), private: one typed method per operation of each schema, with its models, generated by scripts/operations.py. Method names derive from the path and the HTTP method, since the schemas have no operation identifiers.
  • Objects (src/aioovh/<area>/), public: business areas, collections, references and loaded objects, generated by scripts/objects.py from the operations and mapping.yaml.

The hand-written runtime is _client.py (signature, clock offset, OAuth2, retries), _objects.py (collections, references, binding, bounded loading), _root.py (OVH), _settings.py, _endpoints.py, _errors.py, _models.py and _enums.py.

items.title: The mapping
items.text:
mapping.yaml lists every API root, as a path:

  • a collection root (/me/bill: {namespace: billing, name: bills}) starts a collection named name in the namespace;
  • an area (/me: {namespace: account, area: true}) is not a resource: its sub-paths become collections and methods of the namespace, and a GET on the area itself is what await ovh.account returns;
  • a scope (scope: {serviceName: project}) turns a path parameter of the root into a keyword with a default from the settings: the Public Cloud project;
  • a prefix puts a word in front of an area's names when two areas of a namespace would clash (managed for the v2 managed databases next to the 1.0 ones, public_cloud for the v2 Public Cloud areas, in BETA).

The longest matching root wins, so /me/bill goes to billing while the rest of /me goes to account. A root left out of the mapping stops the generator.

items.title: Placement of each operation
items.text:
Under a root, a static segment followed by a parameter is a resource (/me/bill/{billId}). Then:

  • on the item path: GET loads, PUT is update, DELETE is delete; a second GET (from the other API version) is details;
  • on the collection path: a GET returning a list is the iteration, POST is create;
  • a static sub-path with items is a sub-collection (bill.details); one without items is a method named after it (service_infos(), update_service_infos(), reboot()), or an iterable listing when it returns a list;
  • deprecated operations stay in the operations layer only.

A GET that needs more than the identifier (a required query parameter) is a method, not the load.

items.title: Lists of identifiers
items.text: Most 1.0 lists return identifiers. Iterating a collection loads each object, max_concurrency at a time in a task group that ends before the next batch: no task outlives the async for. ids() skips the loading.

items.title: Types and dates
items.text:
datetime fields are whenever.Instant, date fields whenever.Date; a datetime query filter also accepts a Date. Path parameters typed as an enum, a date or an integer are converted from the key, which holds strings. Every model is rebuilt at the end of its module, so that loaded classes in another module inherit resolved fields.

Each schema is self-contained, so shared models such as order.Price exist once per schema that uses them; an area's types module prefixes a name with its API (MeOrderPrice) when two schemas of the area define it.

items.title: Requests
items.text: Each request is built, then signed on its exact URL and body; each retry is signed again. The clock offset is read once from /auth/time. With client_id and client_secret, an OAuth2 token is used instead and renewed 30 seconds before it expires.

items.title: Retries
items.text: Idempotent methods are retried on 429, 502, 503, 504 and transport errors; a POST only on 429, 503 or a connection that never opened.

items.title: Design and roadmap
items.text: aioovh is developed in the open. This page states what it aims at, what it leaves out, and what comes next. Discussion happens in the GitLab issues.

items.title: Principles
items.text:
1. Async only. No synchronous twin of the API: one way to do each thing.
  2. Objects, not paths. The public surface follows what you manipulate; /me, /cloud/project and API versions are details of the routing.
  3. Types first. If the type checker cannot follow it, it is not the API.
  4. Everything reachable. Every operation OVHcloud publishes is either an object method or explicitly left to the raw layer.
  5. Generated, then reviewed. The code is generated from the schemas the API serves; mapping.yaml places every API root in a business area, and the generator stops on a root it does not know or on a name clash.

items.title: Two layers
items.text:
• Operations (aioovh._operations), private: one typed method per operation of each schema.
  • Objects (aioovh.billing, aioovh.compute...), public: business areas, collections, references and loaded objects, generated from the operations and mapping.yaml.

The architecture page details the mapping and how operations become objects.

items.title: Non goals
items.text:
• A synchronous client.
  • Deprecated operations in the object layer: they stay reachable through ovh.raw.
  • Hiding the API: ovh.raw keeps the official package's get, post, put and delete on any path.

items.title: Roadmap
items.text: Step Content 0.1 Every API as objects, collections, references, actions, bounded loading, typed errors, retries 0.2 wait_until(...) on tasks and services with a life cycle 0.3 References from fields that name another resource, plural names reviewed area by area 0.4 Documentation examples executed by the test suite, recipes for FastAPI and task workers later A shared core with aioscaleway, then other European providers

items.title: Prior art
items.text: aioovh stands on what others built: the official OVHcloud package for the signature, the endpoints and the error names, the Stainless generated SDKs for the resource tree, hcloud-python for bound objects, and the Azure SDK design guidelines for versions and paging.

items.title: Async down to the socket
items.text:
The official ovh package is synchronous: each client.get(...) blocks the event loop of a FastAPI application or a task worker while it waits for OVHcloud, and returns a plain dict.

aioovh keeps one httpx2.AsyncClient per OVH object and awaits every request. It signs each one with the $1$ signature on the exact URL and body sent, adding the clock offset it reads once from /auth/time, or sends an OAuth2 bearer token obtained with client credentials.

items.title: Business objects, not paths
items.text:
OVHcloud's paths follow its own history: bills under /me/bill, Public Cloud instances under /cloud/project/{serviceName}/instance, a newer v2 tree next to version 1.0. aioovh exposes what you manipulate instead:

You write You get Requests ovh.billing.bills a collection none ovh.billing.bills.filter(date_from=Date(2026, 10, 1)) the same collection, narrowed none async for b in ovh.billing.bills loaded objects the list, then one per object ovh.billing.bills(bill_id) a reference none await ovh.billing.bills(bill_id) a loaded object one await ovh.compute.vps(name).reboot() the action's result one [i async for i in ovh.billing.bills.ids()] identifiers only one

A loaded object is a reference too. A reference does not load itself when printed or read, because those are synchronous; mypy flags a field read on a bare reference.

items.title: Lists of identifiers, loaded for you
items.text: Most 1.0 lists return identifiers only. Iterating a collection loads each object, max_concurrency at a time (8 by default, OVH_MAX_CONCURRENCY), in a task group that ends before the next batch: no task outlives your async for. ids() skips the loading. The v2 lists return objects and page with a cursor, followed for you.

items.title: Business areas
items.text:
Area What it holds compute dedicated servers, VPS, Public Cloud instances, images and flavors storage, backup NAS-HA, Ceph, NetApp, Public Cloud volumes and object storage, Veeam network IP blocks, IP load balancers, vRack, OVHcloud Connect, CDN, Public Cloud networks kubernetes, databases, analytics, ai managed Kubernetes and registries, managed databases, analytics, AI notebooks and jobs email, domains, web_hosting email offers, domains and DNS zones, web hosting and CMS observability, iam Logs Data Platform, IAM policies, KMS, API applications and SSH keys account, billing, orders the account itself, bills, refunds, payments, services, carts and catalog telecom, licenses, virtualization telephony, SMS, xDSL, software licenses, VMware and Nutanix

The full tree, with every collection and action, is on the object tree page.

items.title: Public Cloud, scoped by project
items.text: Public Cloud resources live in a project. Their collections take project= in filter() and in the call that builds a reference, and fall back to default_project (OVH_DEFAULT_PROJECT).

items.title: Strongly typed, end to end
items.text:
• Every argument, field and result is typed, and the package is checked with mypy --strict in CI.
  • Responses are Pydantic models; dates are whenever.Instant and whenever.Date, and a date filter also takes a Date.
  • Enumerations are open: a value OVHcloud adds later is accepted instead of failing the response.

items.title: Reliable by default
items.text: Throttling and transient failures are retried with stamina, each attempt signed again; a POST is only retried when OVHcloud cannot have processed it. API errors are typed (ResourceNotFoundError, NotGrantedCallError, InvalidCredentialError...) and keep OVHcloud's message and query id.

items.title: Complete
items.text: The code is generated from the schemas the API serves, committed in the repository: 70 APIs of version 1.0 and 18 of v2, about 7,300 operations. Every operation is reachable, through the objects or through ovh.raw, and the coverage page says where.

items.title: Privacy and cookies
items.text: This site sets no cookie, runs no analytics and loads no third party font or script.

items.title: What your browser stores
items.text:
• Your color scheme choice (light, dark or system), in localStorage (__palette), so the next page keeps it.
  • The star and fork counts of the repository shown in the header, in sessionStorage (__source), so they are fetched once per visit.

Neither leaves your browser.

items.title: Who receives your requests
items.text:
• GitLab Pages (GitLab Inc., United States) serves every page and, like any web server, receives your IP address and browser details with each request.
  • The GitLab API (gitlab.com, GitLab Inc.) answers the two requests your browser sends for the repository shown in the header (its star and fork counts, and its latest release), and receives your IP address with them.

See the GitLab privacy statement.
